valueFormat: [value, minus, plus] with the interval type given per value

objects.name: Sirius B
objects.massMethod: dynamical mass from the visual-binary orbit (HST and ground-based astrometry)

measurements.quantity: gravitational redshift of Hα (as a velocity)
measurements.method: HST/STIS Hα of Sirius B measured relative to Sirius A in the same orbit
measurements.note: The authors infer 1.017 ± 0.025 M☉ from it, matching the dynamical mass.

objects.name: Procyon B
objects.massMethod: dynamical mass from the visual-binary orbit (HST astrometry)
objects.radiusMethod: model-atmosphere radius of Provencal et al. (2002) adjusted to the adopted parallax

objects.name: 40 Eridani B
objects.massMethod: dynamical mass from the 40 Eri BC orbit (Mason et al. 2017, USNO), as quoted
objects.radiusMethod: model-atmosphere analysis with the measured flux and parallax

objects.name: Stein 2051 B
objects.massMethod: relativistic deflection of a background star’s image (astrometric microlensing, Sahu et al. 2017), as tabulated
caveats: The mass comes from gravitational lensing, the effect modelled in Gate 6.3.

objects.name: PSR J0740+6620
objects.massMethod: Shapiro delay in radio timing of the binary pulsar (68.3 % credibility)
objects.radiusMethod: equatorial circumferential radius from NICER and XMM-Newton pulse-profile modelling
caveats: A rapidly spinning millisecond pulsar: the star is oblate and its exterior is only approximately Schwarzschild.
An independent analysis of the same X-ray data (Riley et al. 2021) gives a different radius; only Miller et al. is bundled.

objects.name: PSR J0030+0451
objects.radiusMethod: equatorial radius from the same NICER analysis

measurements.method: constrained directly by the pulse profile, more tightly than M and R separately

caveats: A millisecond pulsar: rotation makes the star oblate; the analysis uses an oblate-star exterior, not pure Schwarzschild.

objects.name: PSR B1913+16 (Hulse–Taylor pulsar)
objects.massMethod: relativistic periastron advance and time dilation measured by 35 years of pulsar timing

measurements.quantity: observed / predicted orbital decay from gravitational waves
measurements.method: period derivative corrected by a kinematic term

objects.name: Sagittarius A*
objects.massMethod: stellar orbits around Sgr A* (VLTI/GRAVITY Collaboration 2022), as tabulated by the EHT
objects.shadowMassMethod: stellar orbits (independent of the EHT image)

measurements.method: from the ring with a calibration factor from simulations

measurements.quantity: shadow deviation δ from Schwarzschild (VLTI prior)
measurements.method: shadow diameter compared with the stellar-orbit θ_g

measurements.quantity: mass from the EHT image alone
measurements.method: angular gravitational radius with a maser distance

caveats: Distance uncertainty combines the published statistical (9 pc) and systematic (33 pc) errors in quadrature.
Spin is not modelled; for a Kerr hole the shadow is 0–8 % smaller (−0.08 ≤ δ ≤ 0, EHT).

objects.name: M87*
objects.massMethod: EHT ring size calibrated with GRMHD and geometric models (assumes general relativity)
objects.shadowMassMethod: stellar dynamics (Gebhardt et al. 2011, re-derived by the EHT), independent of the image

measurements.method: EHT 1.3 mm VLBI images (all methods combined)
kinematics of the gas disc (Walsh et al. 2013), as quoted
measurements.note: Predicts a much smaller shadow (21.3 µas, EHT) than observed.

caveats: The EHT mass is derived from the ring itself, so only the stellar-dynamics mass gives an independent prediction.
Spin changes the shadow by up to 4 % (EHT Paper I).

objects.name: Cygnus X-1
objects.massMethod: radio-astrometric distance combined with optical orbital data of the binary
caveats: Spin is not modelled (Schwarzschild values only).
Too distant and small for its shadow to be imaged; no angular comparison.

objects.name: GW150914 remnant
objects.massMethod: gravitational waveform of a binary black-hole merger (source frame)
caveats: The remnant spins (a ≈ 0.67): its horizon and ISCO differ from the Schwarzschild values shown.
